_: Level 1, authored at roadmap 4.6 step 2 to reproduce the level the runtime
used to carry in LEVEL1_DATA. Every number below is MEASURED from the
build at main 28bd1e7 and recorded in docs/diagnostics/
level-1-baseline-timeline.json and -probe.json:
* sector 1 runs 272 rows, because the capital became DUE at active
gameplay frame 600 and the world row at that frame on MEDIUM is 270
(600 * 9/20). 272 is the nearest 8-row module boundary and is the row
the probe's MEDIUM capital actually admitted on (owner decision 3,
plan section 11 item 3).
* the capital traversal itself is 542 rows on every difficulty, so the
two space sectors behind it run 1448 rows each and the level ends at
row 3710 against today's 3712 - the two rows the 8-row module grid
cannot express.
* seed 109 is $6D, which director_c_init XORs with DIFFICULTY_SETTING,
so all three of today's RNG streams are unchanged.
* spacing 24 is the Heavy CLASS FLOOR, deliberately: it puts the wave's
own pacing under the kernel's admission retry (48/36/24 frames by
difficulty), which is what paced the stream before, so the first four
formations land on frames 1, 64, 127 and 190 against 1, 64, 129, 192.
What could NOT be reproduced, and why, is recorded in docs/STATUS.md: the
retired smoke scheduler alternated Raider and Bomber on EVERY admission,
and a WaveDef names ONE archetype while the core page holds 20 waves, so
41 alternating formations cannot be written as 41 waves. This level
alternates in BLOCKS instead - four and four before the capital, six and
six after it - which keeps the density and the cadence and loses the
order. The repository always called that order smoke scheduling and not a
gameplay contract.
